PTMC FINAL REPORT
TEAM NAME: PLANT THE MOON GREEN TEAM
TITLE: What order of compost, soil, and regolith will grow the most and healthiest lettuce?
TEAM ID: 17837
COACH NAME: TRACY F. HENDERSON
DIVISION: ELEMENTARY
Hypothesis:
We think that differently layering the compost, soil, and regolith will
help the lettuce grow healthy and strong!
Original Experimental Parameters and Crops:
Dependent, Independent, and Control
Variables:
Since our experiment is going to take place in a school classroom,
we will not be able to test some of the variables such as the
temperature. We were going to choose different plants as the
independent variable but we chose to change the layering because
we think it will have the best impact on the plant's growth. Lettuce
that is healthier normally is bigger in diameter and taller. So we think
we will measure our plant’s height
We chose lettuce because it was the only plant we researched that
worked with the constraints and criteria. Lettuce is healthy because it
has 82% of the daily value of vitamin A and we thought the
astronauts should eat healthy. We needed to find a plant that is small
and Portable and does not weigh much. Lettuce doesn't need a lot of
water so the crew won’t have to bring a lot of water.
We chose our control variables because those are certain things
about our plants’ needs that we did not want to change and we
researched the water, light, humidity, PH level, and temperature that
lettuce plants need. On the moon, there are 2 weeks of light and 2
weeks of dark. That is why we are using the grow lights as a control
